facts.statement: Mandschurosaurus is an extinct genus of hadrosaurid dinosaurs named "lizard from Manchuria" based on fossils from China and possibly Laos.
facts.quote: Mandschurosaurus (meaning "lizard from Manchuria") is an extinct genus of hadrosaurids based on material from the Late Cretaceous of China and possibly also the Early Cretaceous of Laos.

facts.statement: Mandschurosaurus holds the distinction of being the first dinosaur genus ever named from China.
facts.quote: It was the first dinosaur genus named from China.

facts.statement: The holotype of Mandschurosaurus amurensis is a poorly preserved skeleton collected by Russian scientists in 1914 from the banks of the Amur River in China.
facts.quote: The holotype of M. amurensis (IVP AS coll.), the only valid species within the genus, is based on a poorly preserved and incomplete skeleton collected by Russian scientists in 1914 from the banks of the Amur River, China

facts.statement: The holotype was originally described as Trachodon amurense by Riabinin in 1925 before being reassigned to the new genus Mandschurosaurus in 1930.
facts.quote: The holotype material was initially referred to the genus Trachodon (a nomen dubium) as T. amurense by Riabinin (1925), but was later reassigned to a new genus by Riabinin (1930).

facts.statement: A mounted skeleton of the holotype is displayed at the Central Geological and Prospecting Museum in St. Petersburg, though much of it is made of plaster.
facts.quote: A mounted skeleton based on the holotype of M. amurensis is on display at the Central Geological and Prospecting Museum in St. Petersburg, although much of the skeleton is plaster.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Mandschurosaurus measured 11.24 meters long, 6.48 meters tall, and weighed between 1.5 and 2 metric tons.
facts.quote: While the holotype of M. amurensis would have measured 8 m long and 4.5 m tall, the largest specimen would have measured 11.24 m long and 6.48 m tall and weighed around 1.5-2 metric tons (3,300-4,400 pounds).

facts.statement: The validity of the genus Mandschurosaurus is debated, with some researchers considering it a nomen dubium while others regard it as a valid taxon.
facts.quote: There has been some debate regarding the validity of this genus. Brett-Surman (1979) first considered it a nomen dubium, though some later workers have continued to see it as a valid taxon (Chapman et Brett Surman, 1990, for example). Most recently, Horner et al. (2004) listed the type species as a nomen dubium in the second edition of The Dinosauria.

facts.statement: Mandschurosaurus is most often classified within the family Hadrosauridae as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Within Ornithopoda, Mandschurosaurus is most often placed within Hadrosauridae as a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Mandschurosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago, in the Campanian stage of Asia.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense de Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Mandschurosaurus were found on the right bank of the Amur River near Blagovéshchensk, Russia.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la ribera derecha del Río Amur, Blagovéshchensk, Rusia.

facts.statement: The first species collected, Mandschurosaurus amurensis, was found in 1914 and formally described in 1930 by Riabinin.
facts.quote: La primera especie colectada Mandschurosaurus amurensis, se encontró en el año 1914 y fue descrito en 1930 por Riabinin.

facts.statement: Several species have historically been assigned to the genus Mandschurosaurus, including M. mongoliensis, M. jiainensis, and M. laosensis.
facts.quote: A través de los años varias especies se han referido al género Mandschurosaurus amurensis, Mandschurosaurus mongoliensis, Mandschurosaurus jiainensis y Mandschurosaurus laosensis.

facts.statement: Research suggests that M. mongoliensis is a synonym of Gilmoreosaurus and M. laosensis may be a nomen dubium that was not actually a hadrosaurid.
facts.quote: Horner et al. en 2004 consideran a M. mongoliensis como sinónimo de Gilmoreosaurus y M. laosensis como nomen dubium y posiblemente no haya sido un hadrosáurido.

facts.statement: Mandschurosaurus belongs to the subfamily Hadrosaurinae, the family Hadrosauridae, and the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hadrosaurinae Family: Hadrosauridae Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The time range for Mandschurosaurus spans from the Aptian to the Maastrichtian, between 121.4 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Maastrichtian (121.4 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Mandschurosaurus possessed a broad, flat beak and a long tail, features similar to other hadrosaurs.
rejected.quote: It had a broad, flat beak and a long tail, similar to related hadrosaurs.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a broad flat beak and a long tail'
